searches.note: Twenty three searches of twenty eight, five unspent. Six were restricted to a house's own domain (Aquitania twice, De Martino twice, Roberto Henríquez twice); others blocked the author's main sources. No WebFetch was tried.

method: Each record read with one instruction, refute it: dates, people, grapes, sites, making, ageing, serving, label, story, cards and questions, then the house rules.
Each change below gives what was, what is now and why in one sentence; the sources listed per record are the refuter's own.
Edits made in place; the fragment lints sound with five records refuted.

tested: Founding 1934 and Pietro De Martino from Italy, four generations, the 1996 Carmenère: the house's own pages. Sound.
First vintage 2011: Dhall and Nash, Opici, Berry Bros and the reviews; the house's 2021 programme counts 2021 the tenth vintage. Kept, left open.
Tinajas bought in 2010, fourteen jars: no source. Cut.
Secano Interior labelling: the 2015 decree (BCN) and Berry Bros 2014. Changed.
Guarilihue granite and quartz, ungrafted, dry farmed, destemmed, semi carbonic, no oak, 1982 vineyard: the 2018 sheet and two merchants. Sound.

changes.change: story and questions[1].exp: the family buying tinajas in 2010 and fourteen jars in the first vintage were found in no source read; cut, the 2011 first vintage kept (Dhall and Nash, Opici, Berry Bros).

story and label: early vintages were all labelled Secano Interior was not so (the 2011 and 2012 carry Itata on reviews); now some vintages were sold as Secano Interior until the decree of 2015 opened the Itata name to Cinsault (Decree 7 of 2015, Berry Bros 2014).
sources: the Les Caves de Pyrene blog replaced by the 2015 decree and a merchant's focus page.

sources.title: Library of the National Congress of Chile: Decree 7 of 2015
Dhall and Nash: the Viejas Tinajas wines of De Martino
Berry Bros and Rudd: De Martino Viejas Tinajas Cinsault 2014

open: The house's 2021 programme calls the 2021 the tenth vintage of Viejas Tinajas, which would start the series in 2012; three merchants and the reviews give 2011. The record keeps 2011.
Recent vintages appear as Viejas Tinajas Tinto with some whole bunches, as the author reported.

tested: Founded 2011 by two who met teaching at the Universidad de Concepción, a garage in the city: Primal, Mysa, Skurnik summaries. Sound, borrowed cut.
Cinsault about 95 per cent with País, vines of 1960, La Bella at Guarilihue on granite, concrete fermentation, twelve months in concrete on the sheet; neutral oak on later retail notes. Changed.
Grand Itata Blanco: Colina Sur 1922, Moscatel, Riesling, Sémillon in some years (Cream, Bowler, Brazos). Sound.

changes.change: making, table, story and cards[1]: raised for about a year in concrete with no oak was told as fixed; the sheets read give twelve months in concrete for older vintages, while retailers' notes of 2018, 2021 and 2022 speak of neutral oak, so no oak is cut and the concrete is tied to the sheets read; three weeks on the skins and no temperature control were found nowhere and are cut.
sites: granite and quartz with some clay is now granite, and the vineyard is named La Bella (Brazos sheet and listing).
story: a borrowed garage is now a garage, the sources differing on borrowed or one car; meeting at the Universidad de Concepción confirmed (Primal, Mysa).

sources.title: Brazos Wine: Rogue Vine Grand Itata Tinto 2018
Highbury Vintners: Rogue Vine Grand Itata Tinto 2021
Cream Wine Company: Rogue Vine Grand Itata Blanco 2022

open: The house's own page gives a blend of Cinsault, País and Carignan for a Grand Itata Tinto, against Cinsault with five per cent País on the importers' sheets; the record follows the sheets.
The Super Itata Tinto's grapes remain unconfirmed, as the author reported.

tested: 1984 search, 1990 land at Quebrada de Macul, cellar 1993, Traiguén planted 1993, first Sol de Sol 2000, Champagne partner January 2002: the house's history and vineyard pages, Vine Connections. Sound.
The father in law, not the wife's family: the house. Changed.
Making: whole bunch, nine months in oak, a tenth new, a small part through malolactic (Botilia); larger barrels and stirring found nowhere. Changed.
Six hundred kilometres: found nowhere. Cut. Soil: deep red volcanic clay by the house, clay and granite on its sheets. Changed.
Sol de Sol Pinot Noir: the house's wine and vineyard pages. Added.

changes.change: making, glass, table and questions[0]: barrels larger than the standard size and lees stirring were found in no source read and are cut; whole bunch pressing, nine months in oak, a small share new and a small part through malolactic rest on a merchant's sheet and the house's account.

sites, table, story and cards[0]: some six hundred kilometres south of Santiago found in no source; now south of the Bío Bío, the house's words that no vineyard then grew further south; the soil set to the house's deep red volcanic clay, with granite on its sheets.

story: the Chilean partner worked with his father in law, by the house, not his wife's family; the two Bordeaux founders are described as they were then, the owner of Cos d'Estournel and the director of Château Margaux.
others: Sol de Sol Pinot Noir added from the house's pages (the author found it unconfirmed); sources: the South America Wine Guide replaced by a merchant's sheet.

sources.title: Viña Aquitania: Valle del Malleco, Traiguén

open: The year of the Valle del Malleco decree was not found; the house's claim that the wine led to it is told as its account.
The first Sol de Sol of 2000 was bottled under the Domaine Paul Bruno label by one account; not taught.

tested: 1776 and seven generations: Jenny and Francois, The Grape Reset, Primal (1760s). Sound, hedged.
Name from the Mapuche: the importer's page alone, the family's account. Kept hedged, open.
Raulí vats, unfined, unfiltered, no added sulphur, the litre bottle: Primal, Cream, 67 Wine. Sound.
Trumao over lava: one importer; trumao glossed by a university paper. Lava cut.
Vino Naranja and Naturalmente Tinto: Cream, Leon and Son, 67 Wine disagree. Narrowed.

changes.change: sites and cards[1]: over an ancient lava flow rests on one importer's page alone and is cut; trumao kept as the family's description, the word glossed by a Chilean university paper.
label: Secano Interior now teaches the 2015 decree that lets País and Cinsault carry it (Decree 7 of 2015).

others: the Vino Naranja's two months in raulí rests on one sheet, another gives two to three weeks; now a skin contact white of Moscatel in most vintages; the Naturalmente Tinto now several grapes fermented together.
sources: two retail pages replaced by an importer's profile (1776, seven generations) and the decree; 1776 now rests on two importers besides the author's.

sources.title: Jenny and Francois Selections: Cacique Maravilla
Library of the National Congress of Chile: Decree 7 of 2015
Cream Wine Company: Cacique Maravilla Vino Naranja 2022

open: The name's origin, given by the Mapuche to a forebear, rests on the family's account through its importer alone; told as the family tells it.
The family's winery was destroyed in the earthquake of 2010 by several retail accounts; not taught.

tested: Born Concepción, agronomist of the Universidad de Concepción, Chile, South Africa, Canada and France, the Mosse family of Anjou, Luyt, May 2015: the house's biography and Wines Under the Bonnet. Sound.
Rented vineyards: the house has a page of its own vineyards. Changed.
Rivera del Notro Tinto: País, Nacimiento, 800 metres from the river, alluvial, two hundred years by the house; vessels differ by sheet (C Europa, Stanley's, RAW WINE). Changed.
Blanco: Moscatel, Chasselas called Corinto, Sémillon, by the house. Changed.

changes.change: making and table: hand destemming and a year mostly in concrete with a small part in old barrels came from one retailer, and the concrete and barrel figure belongs to the Blanco and the orange wine; the Tinto's sheets give steel, or concrete then steel; now neutral vessels with no new oak.

story and traps[2]: vineyards he rents rather than owns is refuted by the house's own page of its own vineyards; now many on long agreements with their owners; organic and biodynamic without certification narrowed to organic (C Europa); the trap now teaches Nacimiento against the denomination.

others: the Blanco is Moscatel, Chasselas called Corinto and Sémillon by the house, its Itata origin unconfirmed and cut; Santa Cruz de Coya's two hundred years cut; the Pipeño, unconfirmed, replaced by País Franco (two importers).

sources: Afar and wine.com replaced by the house's biography and an importer's sheet; Concepción, the university, the Loire with a grower of Anjou and May 2015 confirmed by the house and Wines Under the Bonnet.

sources.title: Roberto Henríquez: Rivera del Notro Blanco
C Europa: Rivera del Notro Tinto sheet
Wines Under the Bonnet: Roberto Henriquez

open: The vineyard's soil: alluvial in all accounts, over black basaltic sand in one; the record says alluvial over dark sand.

livingNamesMet: The two founders of Rogue Vine, the grower of Cacique Maravilla, the third and fourth generations of the De Martino family, the living founders and partners of Viña Aquitania, the Loire grower and the French winemaker in Chile beside Roberto Henríquez: none named in prose. The founder of Viña Aquitania who died in 2016 is described, not named.

For people.json, by the read together agent: Leonardo Erazo, Justin Decker, Manuel Moraga Gutiérrez, Bruno Prats, Felipe de Solminihac, Ghislain de Montgolfier, René Mosse, Louis-Antoine Luyt, Marco Antonio De Martino, Sebastián De Martino.

swaps.ruling: No swap. The plan's note on a Sol de Sol Pinot Noir is answered: it exists by the house's pages and is now in others. The Viejas Tinajas Tinto rename of recent vintages is noted for the integrator; the plan's name stays, as the long standing label.

questions: All ten questions have one right answer, four options of one kind and an explanation naming the nearest wrong option; Aquitania's wine question key changed from nine months on its lees to nine months in oak, and De Martino's story explanation no longer teaches 2010.
codexTension: The library record of De Martino (p-de-martino) is not in tension. The region record counts the Malleco with Itata and Bío Bío, which the Aquitania record follows; it is a separate valley of the Southern region, which the trap says.
